extracted.intended_audience: Entities and individuals participating in FCC programs (e.g., USF, TRS, NDBEDP, ACP), their legal counsel and compliance officers, FCC staff (SDO, program administrators), and other stakeholders affected by suspension/debarment rules
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule adopting OMB governmentwide nonprocurement suspension and debarment Guidelines and FCC-specific supplemental rules, procedures, and remedies (including Limited Denial of Participation) applicable to Covered Programs. The document defines scope, causes, evidentiary standards, processes, participant tiers, durations, and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB Guidelines as framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts the Office of Management and Budget's Guidance for Nonprocurement Debarment and Suspension (the Guidelines) as the framework for FCC suspension and debarment rules, along with agency-specific supplemental rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption incorporates the Guidelines' broader range of misconduct that can trigger exclusions, the governmentwide reach of remedies, and the Guidelines' procedural structure (subparts F, G, H). The FCC tailors supplemental rules to its Covered Programs and coordinates placement in 2 CFR part 6001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'suspension' is an action that immediately prohibits a person from participating in covered transactions for a temporary period, pending completion of an investigation and any judicial or administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension has prospective but immediate effect; it usually precedes notice and a chance to be heard; SDO may impose suspension only when it finds 'immediate action is necessary to protect the public interest.' Suspension is typically capped at 12 months (may extend additional 6 months) and may continue if legal/debarment proceedings initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'debarment' is an action to exclude a person from participating in covered transactions for a specified period as a final determination that the person is not presently responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debarment is imposed after notice and an opportunity to contest; typically effective following a 30-day opportunity to respond and issuance of a final order. Period typically should not exceed three years, though SDO may extend or impose additional requirements (e.g., petition for readmission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards for remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Different evidentiary standards apply: 'adequate evidence' supports suspension and LDP; 'preponderance of the evidence' is required for debarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDO must find 'adequate evidence' to support a suspension or LDP and 'preponderance' to impose debarment. Filing of a criminal indictment or information constitutes adequate evidence for an LDP. For suspensions, immediate action requires finding immediate necessity to protect public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-punitive character of exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension and debarment are administrative, prospective actions taken to protect government business interests, not punitive, and are separate from civil enforcement, criminal prosecutions, or debt collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions do not replace or limit other statutory or enforcement tools; exclusions may occur in parallel with or as a result of other proceedings but are distinct remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and effect of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspension or debarment excludes the suspended/debarred party from new covered transactions governmentwide (procurement and nonprocurement), but may allow continuation of existing transactions that preexisted the exclusion under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants may continue to use services of an excluded person as a principal if those services were in use before exclusion; SDO may also permit limited exceptions when alternate providers are unavailable. The FCC adopts a presumption that SDO will exclude parties from existing transactions subject to reasonable transition periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — Covered Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules apply to nonprocurement transactions only under the FCC's specified Covered Programs (e.g., USF programs, TRS, NDBEDP, ACP Outreach Grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules do not extend to other FCC programs or to transactions to/from licensees with spectrum rights except when they are participants in Covered Programs. Some amendatory instructions are delayed indefinitely; effective dates vary by instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Participants and Participant Tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants include beneficiaries and service providers (Primary Tier) and other entities involved in program implementation (Lower Tier), such as contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, marketing organizations, or agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower-tier persons are not participants unless they (i) have a material role affecting claims for disbursements, (ii) are a 'principal' in the transaction, or (iii) are involved in transactions anticipated to be at least $25,000. The FCC will broadly construe 'involved in' (e.g., assisting in application submission). E-Rate and Rural Health Care beneficiaries that deal directly with the Commission/USAC are treated as participants; Lifeline subscribers and TRS/NDBEDP end-users are not participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes for suspension or debarment (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines' causes include convictions or civil judgments for fraud or offenses indicating lack of business integrity, violations of public agreements/transactions so serious as to affect program integrity, failure to pay substantial debts owed to any Federal agency, and '[a]ny other cause that is so serious or compelling in nature that it affects [the party's] present responsibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may adopt additional causes consistent with the Guidelines; SDO evaluates conduct in light of aggravating/mitigating factors and case-specific circumstances to determine whether the cause affects present responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC-specific supplemental causes (Supplemental Rule 6001.450)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC-specific causes include willful or grossly negligent submission of false/misleading FCC forms or documentation resulting in or risking overpayments; willful or grossly negligent violation of statutory/regulatory provisions applicable to Covered Programs; willful, grossly negligent, or habitual failure to respond to Commission or program administrator information requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all such violations will be serious enough to warrant exclusion; the supplemental rule provides notice of conduct that may, depending on facts and circumstances, be sufficiently serious to affect program integrity. SDO will consider compliance with document retention regulations and the quality/credibility of evidence when evaluating failures to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other FCC causes (single serious violation / non-payment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional causes include a single serious violation of Commission rules or repeated violations, and a single substantial or habitual non-payment/under-payment of Commission regulatory fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'single serious violation' materially and negatively affecting present responsibility may warrant exclusion; these causes bear on present responsibility to do business with the federal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating and mitigating factors (considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: SDO should consider aggravating and mitigating factors as set forth in §180.860 when evaluating whether to impose exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include (by reference) those in §180.860—e.g., seriousness of misconduct, harm caused, repetition, culpability, remediation, self-reporting, cooperation, and steps taken to prevent recurrence. The SDO evaluates the totality of circumstances including whether misconduct was isolated, egregiousness, and whether violator self-reported or remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may impute the conduct of one person to another for purposes of exclusion in the same manner as provided under §180.630.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imputation rules allow attribution of misconduct across organizations and individuals where relevant (e.g., contractors, principals). The same approach applies for LDPs per §6001.1119.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Denial of Participation (LDP) — availability and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An LDP is an alternative remedy to suspension/debarment to address misconduct that may not warrant exclusion, allowing the SDO to limit participation in some or all covered programs or otherwise restrict participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LDP is FCC-specific and applies only to FCC activities; it may be tailored geographically or by program and is designed to address less severe or different misconduct than full suspension/debarment while minimizing disruption to services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes supporting an LDP (§6001.1105)
rubrics_metrics.description: An SDO may issue an LDP based on adequate evidence of any of the following: (1) approval would be an unsatisfactory risk; (2) irregularities in current/past performance; (3) failure to honor contractual obligations or abide by FCC regulations; (4) documented deficiencies in FCC programs; (5) false certification in connection with an FCC program; (6) act/omission that would be cause for debarment under §180.800; (7) violation of law/regulation/procedure relating to an FCC program; (8) making/procuring false statements to influence Commission action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of an indictment or information constitutes adequate evidence for LDP. When evaluating LDP appropriateness, SDO should consider totality of circumstances (isolation vs repeated, egregiousness, self-reporting/remediation). Imposition of an LDP for one FCC program may constitute adequate evidence for concurrent LDPs in other FCC programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of an LDP
rubrics_metrics.description: An LDP extends at minimum to the program(s) under which the cause arose; SDO may extend to other Commission programs and may impose nationwide or geographically limited LDPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If LDP is based on causes in §180.800 (e.g., indictments, convictions, fraud evidence), there is a presumption LDP applies to all Commission programs subject to LDPs unless SDO determines broader application is inappropriate. Participation includes receipt of any financial benefit, loans, guarantees, or other arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: LDP process — notice and opportunity to respond (§6001.1102 & §6001.1113)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before imposing an LDP, the SDO must provide notice that an LDP is proposed; the notice shall state the person has 15 days to respond, specify causes and potential effects (length, programs/geographic areas affected), and explain rights to contest via conference or written opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 15 days of notice, the respondent may request a conference with the SDO and the investigating unit; the conference is held within 15 days unless waived. Alternatively, the respondent may oppose the remedy in writing and file documents within 30 days. SDO must issue a written decision within 30 days after the conference or after any agreed extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: LDP duration and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An LDP may remain in effect initially up to 12 months and may be extended up to an additional six months if necessary to ensure compliance or if misconduct persists or new causes arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During or after the LDP period, the SDO may convert to a suspension/debarment proceeding if additional facts warrant. If parties decline to contest, the LDP becomes effective upon issuance of the order; otherwise it is effective only after conclusion of contest proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative agreements and compliance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: SDO may issue administrative agreements as supplemental remedies or alternatives to LDPs, requiring measures such as compliance agreements to enhance oversight and facilitate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before approving administrative agreements, the SDO shall consult with the bureau/office responsible for affected programs and the Office of General Counsel; any compliance agreement requires OGC approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition and continuation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: SDO shall consider the effect of exclusion (suspension/debarment/LDP) on current customers and fashion orders to minimize service disruptions, including requiring excluded parties to notify customers to ensure smooth transitions to alternative providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where alternate service providers are unavailable, SDO may consider limited exceptions in the public interest; the same transition/continuation considerations apply to suspensions and LDPs (see §6001.310).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity with other federal exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent another federal agency has excluded an entity or individual from its programs, the FCC's revised rules generally provide for reciprocity and exclusion from FCC programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocity promotes governmentwide exclusion from new covered transactions, subject to SDO discretion and supplemental rules regarding exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and notifications upon final LDP
rubrics_metrics.description: When an LDP becomes final or the contest period expires, the SDO shall notify relevant bureaus/offices, OGC, Office of the Managing Director, and relevant program Administrators of the scope of the LDP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDO must ensure internal notification so program administrators and contracting officers are aware of restrictions when considering procurements or program participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on advisory committees and service roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded entities or individuals generally may not serve, or continue to serve, on Commission advisory committees and comparable groups or task forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion orders should state such prohibitions; SDO may require disclosures to other participants that the entity is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process coordination and consolidation between LDP and suspension/debarment proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of proposed debarment or suspension is pending based on the same transaction(s) or conduct as an LDP, LDP proceedings are stayed during the 30-day period to contest the debarment/suspension; contested matters may be consolidated and records transferred into the suspension/debarment proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final debarment/suspension is entered, it will constitute a final decision with respect to the LDP to the extent based on the same conduct; the SDO may consolidate parts of proceedings as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention and evidentiary quality considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating failures to respond or other causes, the SDO will consider compliance with applicable document retention regulations and the quality and credibility of evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence/absence of records and the credibility of proffered evidence bear on whether conduct affects present responsibility and whether exclusion is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement, implementation, and delayed effective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Most supplemental rules codified at 2 CFR part 6001 (and cross-referenced into relevant 47 CFR parts); certain amendatory instructions are effective immediately while others are delayed indefinitely or subject to future Federal Register notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulated parties must track effective dates (e.g., Amendatory instruction 3 effective May 11, 2026; others delayed indefinitely) and consult the published PDF for official format. Some program-specific cross-references and updates require annual reporting or new certification content (e.g., 2 CFR 180.335 information referenced in §64.6207 and §64.6215).
